sources.label: Meta Ad Library
sources.claim: Meta's public Ad Library shows the ads any page is currently running — free, no account, open to everyone. It is the same public archive Five to Nine reads for its checks. (Returns 403 to bots, live in a browser.)

sources.label: Meta Ad Library help
sources.claim: Meta's own help documentation describes the Ad Library as the public surface for ads running across its platforms. It documents no follow button, no save, no alerts, and no export.

sources.label: AdLibrary — Limitations of Meta Ad Library 2026 (May 17, 2026)
sources.claim: A third-party audit of the Meta Ad Library's limits, published May 17, 2026: no saved searches, no export, no alerts, no team workspaces, and commercial ads disappear once inactive. The Ad Library was built for civic transparency, not competitor follow.

sources.label: Apify — jy-labs/meta-ad-library-multi-search-scraper
sources.claim: A scheduled Apify actor that scrapes the Meta Ad Library at $10 per 1,000 results. Its onlyNewAds option delivers new-ad detection across runs; it does not deliver landing-page diff, offer timeline, screenshot proof, or a worth-action verdict.
